It is a 2D barcode type that can store a lot of data, readable even if damaged. At least 1 character is enough (can be numeric or text).
Standard 2D barcode format commonly used for boarding passes and transport tickets. It can store high-density data in small spaces and remains readable even if damaged.
High-density linear barcode supporting letters, numbers, and special characters. At least 1 character required, no length limit.
High-density linear barcode supporting letters, numbers, and special characters. Widely used in logistics, inventory management, and shipping.
A 12-digit numeric barcode used on retail products. Must be exactly 13 digits, no other characters allowed.
The 13-digit numeric barcode seen on products at supermarket checkout systems. Provides a global standard product identity.
A simple barcode used in blood bank and library systems. Requires at least 2 digits or characters, usually accepts 0-9 and A-D.
An older but simple barcode format. Preferred in blood banks, libraries, and some healthcare systems.
One of the first common barcodes supporting letters and digits. Must be at least 1 character, accepts A-Z, 0-9, and some symbols.
One of the first widely used barcodes supporting letters and numbers. Used for many years in the automotive and defense sectors.
A more compact version of Code 39. Must be at least 1 character, supports A-Z, 0-9, and special characters.
An improved, higher density version of Code 39. Used primarily in postal services and corporate inventory management.
2D barcode storing a large amount of data in small spaces. At least 1 character (text or numeric) is sufficient.
2D barcode capable of storing large amounts of data in a tiny size. Frequently used on medicine packaging and electronic components.
A short barcode used on small products. Must be exactly 8 digits, no other characters allowed.
8-digit numeric barcode designed for small packages. Preferred on smaller items to save labeling space.
A barcode used exclusively for numeric data. Must be at least 2 digits, and the digit count must be even (e.g., 02, 1234).
An interleaved numeric-only barcode format. Commonly used on corrugated boxes and transport packaging.
A multi-row 2D barcode used on documents and IDs. At least 1 character is enough, can store thousands of characters.
A multi-row 2D barcode format. Often seen on ID cards, driver\'s licenses, and shipping documentation.
A 12-digit barcode used in the US and Canada. Must be exactly 12 digits, no letters allowed.
12-digit barcode used for retail products in the US and Canada. Most products on supermarket shelves are tagged with this.
A compressed version of UPC-A. Must be exactly 6 digits, expanding to 12 digits in some systems.
A shorter, compressed version of UPC-A. Used on small packages or narrow label areas.
